solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aid to mounting pin-ups got fixed on frame of cork

indicators.note: one piece sits on the next, so the rearranged letters come before the framed ones
letters that are fixed are repaired or rigged, so they get put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of both words, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its outline, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of cork

explanation.surface: Someone pins up glamour pictures on a cork board, which is pictured as helping somebody climb.
explanation.walkthrough: UPPING-STOCK is a step or block used for getting up onto a horse, so the 'mounting' here is climbing into the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounting block is a raised step that helps a rider climb into the saddle, which is exactly an aid for that.

clue.text: Medicinal bark for each one restricted by age

parts.note: per means for each, as in so much per head

indicators.note: something restricted by another thing is hemmed in by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an era is an age
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dose of something per person, limited by how old they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes inside the word for age, and the word for each sits in front of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Pereira is the bark of a Brazilian tree once used in medicine as a tonic and remedy for fever.

clue.text: Hamper contains diminutive one with moulded glass ornament

indicators.note: one word holding another means the second is placed inside the first

parts.note: a ped is a dialect word for a basket or hamper
the smallest of a litter is the runt

explanation.surface: A picnic basket holds a tiny little person along with some decorated glassware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a verb meaning hinder, but it is the basket. A prunt is a blob of glass stuck onto a vessel as decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A prunt is a moulded lump applied to glassware for decoration, so a vessel bearing one is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Reason for infanta's visit (t' retinue having lost heart drifting off)?

indicators.note: letters drifting off wander out of their places, so they are rearranged
losing the heart means the very middle letter of the word drops out

parts.note: the shortened article, a single letter
taken as written, before its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A Spanish princess's attendants, dozing off, explain why she came calling.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'I had a little nut tree' says the King of Spain's daughter came to visit because of that tree. RETINUE loses its central I before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the infanta, the Spanish king's daughter, comes to see the speaker for the sake of the little tree bearing a silver nutmeg.

clue.text: 'To the devil, sirrah!' It's howl e.g. when infuriated (9, two words)

indicators.note: something infuriated is thrown into a wild state, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: every letter of these words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An enraged master yells a curse at his servant, which is described as a kind of howl.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to go whistle is an old dismissive phrase, like telling them to go hang or clear off to perdition.

clue.text: Pack round end of hunt are beginning to mutter quietly

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of hunt
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is used

parts.note: the opening letter of mutter
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A hunting pack, as the chase ends, start grumbling under their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like the hounds of the hunt, but it is a verb. The are is a metric unit of a hundred square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamp is to press material down firmly around something, such as earth around a post or clay around a charge.

clue.text: Round on R & A punctuated by a little socket?

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: a word punctuated by something has that thing breaking into it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the two letters as printed
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: A round of golf at the Royal and Ancient is interrupted by a small hole in the course.
explanation.walkthrough: The R & A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, which suggests a golf round. The small word for a little goes between the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbita is the anatomical term for the bony cavity of the skull that holds the eye, the eye socket.

clue.text: Clouds? You may see risible actors cast in this lost base

indicators.note: actors cast in a play are shuffled into roles, and the letters are likewise recast in a new order
the phrase says the stated letters are found in the answer plus the leftover words, so those words must be taken away

parts.note: every letter of both words, the full set to be rearranged
these letters come out of the full set

explanation.surface: A comic venue where laughable performers are cast, now lost, is pictured.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus the letters of 'lost base' rearrange to give 'risible actors', so take those eight letters away and shuffle the five left.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the plural of cirrus, the thin feathery wisps of ice cloud seen high in the sky.

clue.text: Recognized season's end in gardens

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: Kew Gardens are the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London

indicators.note: a word's end is its last letter, the only one taken

parts.note: the final letter of season

explanation.surface: Someone spots the close of the growing season in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is the famous botanic garden in London; the single letter goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Knew is the past tense of know, in the sense of identifying someone or something on sight, as recognized is.

clue.text: Old violet round cell's beginning to etiolate badly — showing this?

definitions.text: Old violet round cell's beginning to etiolate badly — showing this?

indicators.note: one word placed round others wraps them inside it

parts.note: pance is an obsolete name for the pansy, a kind of violet

indicators.note: letters arranged badly are out of order and need sorting

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, the only one taken

parts.note: the first letter of etiolate

explanation.surface: A wilting old violet whose cells have started to lose their colour displays a certain condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a plant that is etiolating, blanched by lack of light, is showing paleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallescence means a growing pale, which is just what an etiolated plant, starved of light, displays.

clue.text: Player 50% depleted has king to beat

indicators.note: depleted by half means half the word's letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written, before its front half goes
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess player who has lost half their pieces still has the king to defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three of PLAYER's six letters are dropped, leaving its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Yerk is a dialect or archaic verb meaning to strike or lash, so it matches hitting someone.

clue.text: Red-tops scream, 'Section in power's bonkers' (11, two words)

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed among its letters

parts.note: a yell is a scream
s is an abbreviation for section

indicators.note: something bonkers is crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Tabloid headline: a mad faction in government.
explanation.walkthrough: Red-tops are British tabloid newspapers, named for their red mastheads. The extra S goes among the letters of the next word before they are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-tops are sensational popular tabloids, and the yellow press is the long-standing term for sensationalist journalism of that kind.

clue.text: Instrument shortened on keel at Actium?

indicators.note: a word that is shortened has its tail cut off

parts.note: taken as written, before it loses its last letter
carina is Latin for keel, and Actium was a Roman sea battle

explanation.surface: A musical instrument cut down and set on the keel of a ship at the battle of Actium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At Actium' tells you to use Latin, the language of the Romans who fought there. The keel is also why the instrument's name fits: it is shaped like a little goose or boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, often made of clay.

clue.text: Parish priest having retired given time to spout

indicators.note: being given something means having it added on
someone who has retired has gone back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A parish priest who has stepped down is given time to hold forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spout' looks like pompous talk, which a retired priest might do, but here it means to belch out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eruct is to belch, to send gas or matter up and out of the mouth, which is a kind of spouting.

clue.text: With damaged limb has to bind wings of ree or small curlew

parts.note: w is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: binding something means wrapping round it, so it goes inside
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of ree

explanation.surface: An injured wading bird with a hurt leg needs its wings bound, whether it is a ree or a curlew.
explanation.walkthrough: A ree is the female ruff, another wading bird, which makes the surface a bird-rescue scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The whimbrel, spelt this way too, is a smaller relative of the curlew with a striped crown and down-curved bill.

clue.text: Bowler needs good one, great when it penetrates Cyril W's partner?

indicators.note: something that penetrates another goes into it

parts.note: Cyril Washbrook's England opening partner was Len Hutton, written in the same style
gt is the abbreviation for great

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a bowler needs something good, and great things happen when it gets through a batsman's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler aims for a good length, the spot where the ball pitches. Cyril Washbrook and Len Hutton opened the batting for England; 'Cyril W' asks for 'Len H'.
explanation.definitionFit: Length is the distance down the pitch at which a delivery bounces, and a good one is what every bowler seeks.

clue.text: In earth, as of old, ants will get busy without delay

indicators.note: the ants are put in the burial word, going inside it

parts.note: to inter is to put in the earth, to bury

indicators.note: busy creatures scurry about, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
surface padding that marks the answer as a dated word

explanation.surface: Underground, as in olden days, ants set to work right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As of old' marks the answer as a dated word, still used humorously or in law.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is a Latin-derived word meaning immediately or at once, so it matches acting with no hold-up.

clue.text: Scots joint I preferred to English in what precedes this

indicators.note: one thing preferred to another is chosen in its place, so it replaces it

parts.note: the answer to the clue just before, 15 across
Eng is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot chooses a joint of meat, preferring it to English fare.
explanation.walkthrough: The previous answer, LENGTH, has its ENG swapped for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lith is a Scottish and northern word for a joint or limb, also a segment of an orange.

clue.text: Wearing university hat, useless

parts.note: you are in what you are wearing
U is the abbreviation for university
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A comment on a mortarboard: wearing the academic hat achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tile is dated slang for a hat, especially a silk topper.
explanation.definitionFit: Inutile is a rare word from French and Latin meaning of no use or profit, the same as useless.

clue.text: Steam bananas in sloppy food we eat together

definitions.note: a clause standing for the plural noun: people who eat together

indicators.note: one thing in another is put inside it

parts.note: a mess is a dish of soft, sloppy food

indicators.note: going bananas is going crazy, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone steams bananas into a sloppy dish that the household shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like part of the menu, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Messmates are companions who share meals at the same table, especially aboard ship, so they are us eating together.

clue.text: It warns of poor visibility all round, as amid thrashing of gam

definitions.text: It warns of poor visibility all round

indicators.note: something amid other things sits in their middle
something thrashing about flails wildly, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
e.g. means for example, as in 'as' introducing a case

explanation.surface: A foghorn sounds in all directions while a school of whales thrashes about.
explanation.walkthrough: A gam is a school of whales, which fits the seagoing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A megafog is a fog signal with megaphones pointing in several directions, so it sounds a warning all around.

clue.text: Espalier and something to train up it, badly installed?

indicators.note: something installed is set inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a fruit tree is what you train along an espalier
ill means badly, as in ill-made

explanation.surface: A garden frame and the plant trained on it look as though they were badly put in.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' is the espalier: a tree trained up it, with a word for badly installed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A treille is a trellis or lattice for training vines and fruit trees, which is what an espalier frame is.

clue.text: Parrot (maybe) 'e selected and I caged

parts.note: the letter as printed

indicators.note: something caged is shut inside, so one letter goes within the word

parts.note: chose means selected
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cockney explains that he picked a bird and put it in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like the caged bird, but it is a verb: to repeat what you hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To echoise is to echo or repeat sounds back, which is what parroting does, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Ed Stewart in new guise as lender to Scottish house buyer?

indicators.note: a new guise is a new outward form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: every letter of the name, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Broadcaster Ed Stewart reinvents himself as a Scottish mortgage lender.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Stewart was a British radio and TV presenter. A wadset is an old Scots mortgage, and the wadsetter is the creditor holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadsetter in Scots law held land in pledge for a debt, rather like a mortgage lender to a property buyer.

clue.text: Submit square, not quite finishing (6, two words)

indicators.note: not quite there means falling one short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: s is an abbreviation for square
an ending is a finishing

explanation.surface: A town square that is nearly complete is offered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a town square or a fair settlement, but it supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To send in an entry or application is to submit it, handing it over for consideration.

clue.text: Oil lamp from Panama, with a hollow in the centre

indicators.note: something in the centre sits in the middle of the other letters

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Panama
the article as written
a dell is a small wooded hollow

explanation.surface: A lamp brought from Panama, with a recess in its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is the international code for Panama.
explanation.definitionFit: A padella is a shallow dish of oil or fat with a wick, used for illuminations, so it is a kind of oil lamp.

clue.text: Loincloth I had taken up, very warm inside

indicators.note: something inside another sits within it
in a down entry taken up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
hot is very warm

explanation.surface: Someone took up wearing a loincloth because the weather was so hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the cloth worn wrapped round the waist and legs by men in India, a form of loincloth.

clue.text: Artless cordiality twice making one giggle?

definitions.note: the answer is the laugh itself, an interjection or noun

indicators.note: doing something twice means the same piece is written two times in a row
read as art-less, the word says those three letters are left out

parts.note: heart means warmth or cordiality

explanation.surface: Naive friendliness, shown twice over, is enough to make anyone titter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artless' looks like one word meaning naive, but it splits: the letters of art are taken from the warmth word.
explanation.definitionFit: He-he represents a high-pitched snigger or titter, the sound of a giggle written out.

clue.text: Fine for Jock having created a disturbance, led off

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so those letters go

parts.note: to brawl is to fight noisily, causing a disturbance
the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A Scot is fined for starting a fight and then hauled away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty for brawling, but it is the adjective. Jock is a nickname for a Scot, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Braw is Scots for fine, handsome or splendid, as in a braw bricht moonlicht nicht.

clue.text: Molten metal passes through this opening (last second)

indicators.note: putting the last letter second moves it up near the front and pushes the others along

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: Liquid metal flows through a gap, the second to last bit of the casting.
explanation.walkthrough: In GATE the final letter is moved into second place.
explanation.definitionFit: A geat is the channel or hole in a casting mould through which the melted metal is poured.

clue.text: Mid point of suture sewn up as in half cut?

indicators.note: stitching things up joins them in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
on can mean slightly drunk, as half-cut does

explanation.surface: A wound stitched closed in the middle, as if half severed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewn up' and 'half cut' both look like surgery, and both are also slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The nasion is the craniometric point at the middle of the suture between the nasal and frontal bones.

clue.text: Caustic making you tender if spread round middle of toe

indicators.note: letters going round another sit either side of it
something spread is opened out and moved about, so the letters change places

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the central letter of toe

explanation.surface: A burning ointment smeared round a toe leaves it sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making you tender' reads as the effect of the caustic, but tender is only the raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An erodent is a substance that eats away tissue, so it is a corrosive or caustic agent.

clue.text: Gendarme ingests nothing like an acid

definitions.note: describes a particular acid; the answer is the adjective in folic acid

indicators.note: something that ingests another takes it inside

parts.note: flic is French slang for a policeman
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A French policeman swallows nothing that resembles acid.
explanation.walkthrough: A gendarme is a French police officer, and flic is the French slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Folic acid is a B vitamin, so this adjective names the particular acid and describes things related to it.

clue.text: Let's suppose the girl took food, by the sound of it glutted

indicators.note: what something sounds like is how it is heard spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.words: Let's suppose the girl took food
parts.note: say for let's suppose, she for the girl, ate for took food

explanation.surface: Imagine a young woman has eaten until she is completely stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: Say, she and ate run together when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective satiate, now mostly poetic, means filled to the full or sated, the same as glutted.

clue.text: Couples in season changing places, except that mentioned

indicators.note: the word is read as two couples of letters
the two pairs swap positions, the back pair moving to the front

parts.note: seel is an old dialect word for a season or time

explanation.surface: Pairs in the mating season swap partners, apart from the one already named.
explanation.walkthrough: Seel, found in Chambers, means a time or season. Its first two letters and last two letters trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means other or besides, so it refers to anything apart from the thing already spoken of.

clue.text: Wenger changing round Milan team — it produces a tasty stimulant

indicators.note: letters going round another set enclose it
something changing alters its form, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: the manager's name, to be rearranged
Inter Milan is an Italian football club

explanation.surface: Arsène Wenger, the Arsenal manager, reshapes an Italian side and gives it a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsène Wenger was Arsenal's manager; Inter is one of Milan's two big football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintergreen is a plant whose aromatic oil flavours sweets and gum and is used as a tonic, hence a tasty stimulant.
